symbols.rationale: OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DataStoreError custom-store error enum; OpenSwiftData's custom-store shape surfaces errors via SwiftDataError (Sources/OSDCore/SwiftDataError.swift) instead. The enum is part of Apple's custom-store SPI and is not part of OpenSwiftData's parity surface.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DataStoreError.invalidPredicate case; OpenSwiftData's custom stores do not throw this case (they use SwiftDataError.unsupportedPredicate instead). Part of the custom-store error enum that OpenSwiftData does not reimplement.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DataStoreError.preferInMemoryFilter case; OpenSwiftData's custom-store shape (OpenSwiftDataDataStore) does not support the in-memory-filter delegation hook. Part of the custom-store error enum that OpenSwiftData does not reimplement.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DataStoreError.preferInMemorySort case; OpenSwiftData's custom-store shape (OpenSwiftDataDataStore) does not support the in-memory-sort delegation hook. Part of the custom-store error enum that OpenSwiftData does not reimplement.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DataStoreError.unsupportedFeature case; OpenSwiftData's custom stores surface unsupported features via SwiftDataError.unsupportedStore instead. Part of the custom-store error enum that OpenSwiftData does not reimplement.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore class (the Core-Data-backed default store). OpenSwiftData uses its own SQLite-backed runtime store (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Storage/) and has no public DefaultStore class. The class is part of Apple's custom-store SPI.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore.cachedSnapshots; OpenSwiftData has no public DefaultStore class (the member belongs to the non-existent class). Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore.initializeState; OpenSwiftData has no public DefaultStore class. Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore.invalidateState; OpenSwiftData has no public DefaultStore class. Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.

OpenSwiftData's SchemaDescriptor.Entity (Sources/OSDCore/Schema.swift) does not expose inheritedProperties; the lower-level schema-introspection metadata that Apple's Entity provides is a deferred feature. The property is public schema API, not custom-store SPI.
OpenSwiftData's SchemaDescriptor.Entity does not expose inheritedPropertiesByName; the lower-level schema-introspection metadata is a deferred feature.
OpenSwiftData's SchemaDescriptor.Entity exposes attributes/relationships directly but not the storedProperties aggregation; the lower-level schema-introspection metadata is a deferred feature.
OpenSwiftData's SchemaDescriptor.Entity does not expose storedPropertiesByName; the lower-level schema-introspection metadata is a deferred feature.
OpenSwiftData's SchemaDescriptor.Entity does not expose subentities; the lower-level schema-introspection metadata (used by Apple's inheritance system) is a deferred feature.

OpenSwiftData implements FetchResultsCollection.subscript (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Query/FetchResultsCollection.swift) but the validator's name-match scanner does not visit SubscriptExprSyntax, so a subscript call x[i] produces no reference to the display name 'subscript'. The API is implemented; the gap is a scanner limitation, not an implementation gap. Changing the scanner is out of scope.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's HistoryProviding protocol; OpenSwiftData's custom-store shape does not expose a custom-store history-vending protocol (history is handled by the runtime store directly). Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.

OpenSwiftData implements HistoryTombstone.subscript(keyPath:) (Sources/OpenSwiftData/History/History.swift) but the validator's name-match scanner does not visit SubscriptExprSyntax, so the subscript call produces no reference to the display name 'subscript'. The API is implemented; the gap is a scanner limitation.
OpenSwiftData's Schema.Index (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Container/Schema.swift) does not declare a CodingKeys enum; the Codable schema-index conformance is a deferred feature.

OpenSwiftData's Schema.Index does not declare a Types enum; the typed-index overload (#Index<T>(Schema.Index.Types<T>...)) is a deferred feature. The enum is public typed-index API, not custom-store SPI.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's RelationshipCollection protocol (which introduces the PersistentElement associatedtype and the Array/Optional conformance extensions). OpenSwiftData's relationship modeling does not use this protocol. Part of Apple's custom-store/relationship SPI.
OpenSwiftData's Schema (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Container/Schema.swift) does not expose an encodingVersion property; the schema encoding-version API is a deferred feature.
OpenSwiftData's Schema does not expose a schemaEncodingVersion property; the schema encoding-version API is a deferred feature.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's Array.PersistentElement typealias (added by conformance to RelationshipCollection). Because OpenSwiftData has no RelationshipCollection protocol, this typealias does not exist in OpenSwiftData. Part of Apple's custom-store/relationship SPI.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's Optional.PersistentElement typealias (added by conformance to RelationshipCollection). Because OpenSwiftData has no RelationshipCollection protocol, this typealias does not exist in OpenSwiftData.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's underscored SPI _generateCurrentClassBackingData on BackingData. The method is underscored SPI used by Apple's @Model macro expansion internals; OpenSwiftData's BackingData protocol (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Model/BackingData.swift) does not declare it. SPI is internal plumbing not part of the public parity surface.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's underscored SPI _superClassBackingData on BackingData. The method is underscored SPI used by Apple's @Model macro expansion internals; OpenSwiftData's BackingData protocol does not declare it.

OpenSwiftData's DataStore protocol (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Store/DataStore.swift) provides cachedSnapshots(for:editingState:) as a no-op default implementation returning an empty dictionary. The caching behavior is deferred; no parity test can assert observable behavior for the no-op default, so a reference would assert nothing.

OpenSwiftData's DataStore protocol provides initializeState(for:) as a no-op default implementation. The state-hook behavior is deferred; no parity test can assert observable behavior for the no-op default.

OpenSwiftData's DataStore protocol provides invalidateState(for:) as a no-op default implementation. The state-hook behavior is deferred; no parity test can assert observable behavior for the no-op default.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore.HistoryType typealias; OpenSwiftData has no public DefaultStore class. Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's DefaultStore.historyType; OpenSwiftData has no public DefaultStore class. Part of Apple's custom-store SPI.

OpenSwiftData implements ModelActor.subscript(id:as:) (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Model/ModelActor.swift) but the validator's name-match scanner does not visit SubscriptExprSyntax, so a subscript call produces no reference to the display name 'subscript'. The API is implemented; the gap is a scanner limitation.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's PersistentModel.getTransformableValue; transformable-attribute accessor support is a deferred feature. The method is public API, not private SPI.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's PersistentModel.setTransformableValue; transformable-attribute accessor support is a deferred feature.

OpenSwiftData's Unique is a public macro (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Macros.swift), not a class, and the validator's scanner does not visit MacroExpansionExprSyntax, so a #Unique<...> expansion produces no reference to the display name 'Unique'. The Apple SwiftData.Schema.Unique class has no OpenSwiftData equivalent; the macro is the OpenSwiftData analog but is scanner-uncoverable. A compilable reference form that produces a visited node with displayName 'Unique' does not exist (Unique is a macro, not a type).
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's Schema.Index.Types.binary case; the typed-index overload is a deferred feature. The case is public typed-index API.
OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's Schema.Index.Types.rtree case; the typed-index (R-tree) overload is a deferred feature.

OpenSwiftData declares a public macro Unique (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Macros.swift) but the validator's scanner does not visit MacroExpansionExprSyntax, so a #Unique<...> expansion produces no reference to the display name 'Unique'. A compilable reference form that produces a visited node with displayName 'Unique' does not exist (a macro is not a type, so Unique.self does not compile). The macro is implemented but scanner-uncoverable.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's Unique.CodingKeys enum; the Codable conformance for the Unique macro helper is a deferred feature. The display name is 'CodingKeys'; the new parity test deliberately does not reference the bare identifier 'CodingKeys' (it would also cover the allowlisted SwiftData.Index.CodingKeys).

OpenSwiftData declares a _PersistedProperty macro (Sources/OpenSwiftData/Macros.swift) but with a different signature than Apple's; it is internal @Model macro plumbing (the @Model expansion emits @_PersistedProperty attributes). The scanner does not visit AttributeSyntax, so an @_PersistedProperty attribute produces no reference. SPI is internal plumbing not part of the public parity surface.

OpenSwiftData does not reimplement Apple's underscored _TransformablePersistedProperty macro. The macro is underscored SPI for transformable-attribute property expansion; OpenSwiftData has no equivalent. SPI is internal plumbing not part of the public parity surface.
